questions.question: Q1. In an integrated drone build, why can a design that passes every individual subsystem test still fail as a whole?

answers.a: Because the subsystems are electrically isolated from each other
answers.b: Because the subsystems are coupled — a change to one shifts mass, current, heat and endurance in the others
answers.c: Because individual tests are always wrong
answers.d: Because the battery is the only component that matters

explanations.a: Incorrect — the subsystems share mass, current and heat; they are strongly coupled.
explanations.b: Correct — integration fails when the coupled operating point does not satisfy every constraint at once.
explanations.c: Incorrect — the isolated tests are valid; integration adds new coupling constraints.
explanations.d: Incorrect — every component contributes to the coupled result.

questions.question: Q2. Adding a larger battery to increase flight time can paradoxically reduce it. Why?

answers.a: A larger battery outputs less voltage
answers.b: Extra battery mass lowers TWR, raising hover throttle and hover current, which drains capacity faster
answers.c: Larger batteries always have lower capacity
answers.d: The ESC ignores the extra mass

explanations.a: Incorrect — voltage is set by cell count, not size.
explanations.b: Correct — added mass raises the hover power draw, and beyond a point the extra draw outweighs the extra capacity.
explanations.c: Incorrect — larger packs usually have more capacity.
explanations.d: Incorrect — mass directly changes the required hover thrust and current.

questions.question: Q3. A build meets its weight and payload targets but the ESC runs above its thermal limit at hover. Which two concepts must be revisited?

answers.b: ESC power electronics and Thermal Management

explanations.a: Incorrect — the failure is electrical/thermal, not aerodynamic or positioning.
explanations.b: Correct — conduction loss (I²·R) and steady-state temperature rise are the ESC and Thermal Management concepts.
explanations.c: Incorrect — control and structure are unrelated to the overheating cause.
explanations.d: Incorrect — the direct cause is ESC conduction loss and cooling, not capacity.

questions.question: Q4. Which single ratio best summarises whether a loaded aircraft has enough thrust to fly safely?

explanations.a: Incorrect — that describes the battery, not lift capacity.
explanations.b: Correct — TWR = 4·Tmax /(m·g); a loaded TWR below ~2 leaves no control margin.
explanations.c: Incorrect — KV and diameter matter but do not summarise lift capacity alone.
explanations.d: Incorrect — component mass ratios do not describe flight capability.

questions.question: Q5. The capstone mission specifies a maximum all-up weight, a minimum flight time and a required payload. Why is the payload treated as a constraint rather than an option?

answers.a: Because payload mass is negligible and can be ignored
answers.b: Because the mission exists to carry it, so a build that only flies unloaded has not met the requirement
answers.c: Because payload only affects the appearance of the aircraft
answers.d: Because the payload powers the flight controller

explanations.a: Incorrect — the required payload is a substantial fraction of the mass budget and changes every downstream number.
explanations.b: Correct — the aircraft is a means to carry the payload. Verifying an unloaded build answers a question nobody asked.
explanations.c: Incorrect — payload is a mass and a power consequence, not a cosmetic choice.
explanations.d: Incorrect — the payload is a load on the system, not a source of power.

questions.question: Q6. The mission is flown at 300 m density altitude rather than at sea level. What does that change?

answers.a: Nothing, since 300 m is a small height
answers.b: Air density falls, so the same propeller at the same RPM produces less thrust
answers.c: The battery delivers less voltage at altitude
answers.d: The flight controller has to be recalibrated for gravity

explanations.a: Incorrect — it is a modest effect, but it moves thrust in the unhelpful direction and eats margin.
explanations.b: Correct — thrust scales with air density, so a build that just barely lifts at sea level has less margin at altitude.
explanations.c: Incorrect — pack voltage is unaffected by air density.
explanations.d: Incorrect — gravity is effectively unchanged over a few hundred metres.

questions.question: Q7. Why does a heavier motor not automatically produce a better aircraft?

answers.a: Heavier motors are always less powerful
answers.b: It adds thrust but also mass and current draw, which affect TWR, ESC heating and endurance at the same time
answers.c: Heavier motors cannot be fitted to standard frames
answers.d: Motor mass has no effect on the design

explanations.a: Incorrect — larger motors generally produce more thrust; that is not the objection.
explanations.b: Correct — every upgrade propagates. More thrust costs mass, current and heat, and whether it is a net gain depends on the whole coupled system.
explanations.c: Incorrect — mounting is a compatibility question the diagnostics handle separately.
explanations.d: Incorrect — motor mass enters the all-up weight four times over.

questions.question: Q8. What does it mean for a build to be self-consistent?

answers.a: All the components come from the same manufacturer
answers.b: Every subsystem satisfies its own limits at the same shared operating point, rather than each being acceptable in isolation
answers.c: The build uses the cheapest available parts
answers.d: The aircraft is symmetrical about both axes

explanations.a: Incorrect — brand has no bearing on whether the physics closes.
explanations.b: Correct — there is one current, one mass and one hover throttle. Self-consistency means every constraint is met at those actual values, not at convenient assumed ones.
explanations.c: Incorrect — cost is not a constraint in this experiment.
explanations.d: Incorrect — geometric symmetry matters for balance but is not what self-consistency means.

questions.question: Q9. The mission requires positioning capability. Which components satisfy that requirement?

answers.a: A GPS module together with a radio receiver

explanations.a: Correct — the verifier checks for a fitted GPS attachment and a receiver when the mission calls for positioning.
explanations.b: Incorrect — capacity extends endurance but provides no position information.
explanations.c: Incorrect — cooling addresses a thermal constraint, not a navigation one.
explanations.d: Incorrect — propeller stiffness is a structural and aerodynamic property.

questions.question: Q10. Hover throttle is a useful health indicator for a build. What does a very high hover throttle tell you?

answers.a: The aircraft is efficient and well matched
answers.b: Most of the available thrust is already being used just to stay up, leaving little margin for manoeuvre or gusts
answers.d: The propellers are too small for the motors

explanations.a: Incorrect — a high hover throttle is the opposite of a comfortable design point.
explanations.b: Correct — control authority lives in the difference between hover throttle and full throttle. Hovering near the top of the stick means there is almost nothing left to correct with.
explanations.c: Incorrect — a full pack lowers hover throttle slightly, if anything.
explanations.d: Incorrect — undersized propellers are one possible cause among several, not the reading itself.
